title_en: This Refurbished Switch 2 Deal May Be Your Last Chance to Buy a Console Under $400
summary_en: This "grade A" refurbished" Switch 2 console is just $399 ahead of Nintendo's upcoming price hike.
body_en:
Have you picked up a Nintendo Switch 2 yet? Time’s running out, if you want to grab one ahead of the September price hike . Right now you can even save an additional $50 if you take advantage of this “Grade A Refurbished” deal on a Switch 2 console at Woot.
Woot is owned and operated by Amazon, so you don’t have to worry about any funny business in dealing with an unknown retailer. It also comes with a 90-day limited warranty that lets you send it back for a full refund if something's wrong with it.
The “Grade A” refurbishment means, according to Woot, that it has been “inspected and guaranteed to have minimal cosmetic damage & has successfully passed a full diagnostic test which ensures like-new functionality & removal of any prior-user's personal information.”
It’s worth noting that you don’t get the original Switch 2 box when you buy this item. It comes with the console and all the standard accessories, but is packaged in a “generic white or brown box.” If you’re cool with those caveats, this might be the lowest price you’ll find for a Switch 2 in the foreseeable future.
Lately it seems as if Nintendo is the only console maker doing the right things. Sony’s first-party output has been sluggish this generation, and now it’s taking heat for its plan to ditch discs . Microsoft, after falling far behind the past two console generations thanks in part to its failed bet on Game Pass , had a regime change this year, with the new manager trying to put out fires left and right (as well as firing a ton of workers ).
Meanwhile, the AAA game market is shrinking because people just want to play the same handful of games 24/7 (Fortnite, Roblox, Call of Duty, GTA, and Minecraft, specifically).
As usual, Nintendo is marching to the beat of its own bongos. The Switch 2 has been a success , and Nintendo's steady first-party support has kept the platform in the conversation since it launched last year. Games like Splatoon Raiders , Star Fox , and Pokémon Pokopia have gotten killer review scores across the board.
But even Nintendo can’t keep its prices down during the AI-induced RAM crisis . That’s why Nintendo, along with Sony and Microsoft , is raising prices on its consoles. So if you want to get a Switch 2 and you don't want to pay a ton, picking up a refurb unit now is probably your best bet.
